 Levine Leichtman Buys Franchisor
 Private equity firm joins in on home services rollups.
 By Hannah Welk 
 November 16, 2026 
 106 
 Facebook Twitter Linkedin Email Print 
 Care: A home services worker sprays pesticides on shrubs. (Photo courtesy of Levine Leichtman) 
 B everly Hills-based private equity firm Levine Leichtman Capital Partners has folded in a home services franchising platform as its newest portfolio company.
 The $15 billion firm acquired Five Star Franchising , home to eight brands, including Mosquito Shield and 1-800-Packouts , from Princeton Equity Group . Headquartered in Springville, Utah, Five Star is the sixth platform investment for Levine Leichtman’s seventh flagship fund and one of more than 120 portfolio companies the private equity firm has brought on since its founding in 1984.
 Five Star’s existing executive team, led by co-founders Scott Abbott and Chad Jones, will stay on and work with Levine Leichtman as the platform pursues further growth. The financial details of the deal were not disclosed.
 “We look forward to leveraging our extensive experience in the franchising space and working with management to continue to expand unit count, drive strong same-store sales growth, and acquire additional brands,” said Matthew Frankel , managing partner of Levine Leichtman, in a news release.
 The local firm’s past investments in the franchising industry include Dallas-based bakery chain Nothing Bundt Cakes , Tempe-based senior care network SYNERGY HomeCare and Atlanta-based health food chain Tropical Smoothie Cafe .
 Sponsor-to-sponsor handoff 
 Five Star joins Levine Leichtman from Princeton Equity, which backed the franchisor’s founders in 2021 and led the company to a 190% increase in revenue from 2022. A wave of interest from Gen Z and millennial franchising applicants helped spur that growth, the company wrote in an August news release announcing its appearance on the Inc. 5000 list.
 The New Jersey firm added Five Star Floor ing and Decorate With Lights to Five Star’s roster of brands this year. Under Levine Leichtman’s watch, Five Star will look to grow both organically and through acquisitions, Abbott said.
 “We are excited to partner with (Levine Leichtman) and leverage the team’s deep expertise in supporting and successfully growing franchised brands like ours,” Abbott said.
 The sponsor-to-sponsor handoff deepens Levine Leichtman’s bet on consolidation in the home services industry. The opportunity for rollups in the sector is significant, with a February report from McKinsey & Co. estimating that 76% of companies performing services like HVAC installation and electrical work operate independently. The consultancy ballparked U.S. spending on home services at $700 billion and lauded the market as recession-resilient.
 “The home services market … has emerged as a focus sector for investors and entrepreneurs alike,” the report reads. “Growth is expected to rise in the coming years, driven by long-term, embedded trends, such as the rising number of existing homes and the increased outsourcing of home services.”
